text:
Zoe: Heads-up - AureliaHealth wants a 10-day POC (8-day burst + 2-day reserved). Procurement says they will issue a single PO but insist on exec sig on the MSA before PO release. Can we do PO-first for a low-risk POC?
Mark (Legal): We received their redlines — they tightened indemnity cap and added a DPA clause forbidding caching without written consent. As-is we should not accept. Suggest an Appendix limiting cache to ephemeral in-memory KV for POC only and capping retention to 14 days.
Dev (Presales): Pricing sketch for readability:
```
burst-8d: $8,000 flat
reserved-2d-equivalent: $1,200
estimated-tokens: 60k
```
If cache disabled, estimate +30% token usage. Could offer extra 20k trial tokens instead of lowering price.
Priya (Finance): Single PO ok but must include Redwood legal name, remittance address, and EIN. Also we need separate invoice lines for revenue mapping. Send GL codes.
procurement-bot: PO checklist - missing vendor EIN and signature block. Use template with multi-line mapping: https://redwood.co/po-template. Attach vendor W-9 or local tax form.
Zoe: @Mark (Legal) - can we accept Appendix approach and allow PO-first conditioned on Sales Ops flagging it and Security quick-approval? Procurement pressured to close this week.
Mark (Legal): Yes we can do PO-first if Sales Ops marks it "PO-first - legal appendix pending" and Security signs off on SOC2 addendum. Otherwise exec sig needed. Draft Appendix language: "For the duration of the AureliaHealth POC, Redwood may use ephemeral in-memory caching limited to KV entries with retention <= 14 days; no external subprocessor persistent caching permitted."
Dev (Presales): I'll prepare two order-form options: (1) PO-first with Appendix + extra trial tokens, (2) exec-sign-first with original rates.
Priya (Finance): Once draft Order Form posted I'll verify invoice lines and GLs. If PO-first, Finance needs a copy of the PO with vendor fields filled.
Zoe: Plan: upload two-option order form now, request Sales Ops expedited e-sign if exec required, and ping Security for SOC2 addendum thumbs-up. Back shortly. :thumbsup:
